{{Sexagenary cycle}}
'''Yang Wood Rat''' (甲子, ''kinoe nezumi''; onyomi ''kōshi'') is the 1st of the sixty combinations of the {{ill|Sexagenary cycle|af|Sestigdelige siklus|ar|دورة ستينية|arz|دوره ستينيه|as|ষাঠি বছৰীয়া আৱৰ্তন|ast|Ciclu sexaxenariu|bn|ষাটবার্ষিক চক্র|ca|Cicle sexagesimal|cdo|Găng-ciĕ|cs|Kan-č’|de|60-Jahre-Zyklus|eo|Ĉina sesdekjara ciklo|es|Ciclo sexagesimal chino|eu|Hirurogeitaka urteko ziklo|fa|چرخه شصت‌تایی|fr|Cycle sexagésimal chinois|hak|Kôn-chṳ̂|hy|Վաթսունամյա շրջան|id|Ganzhi|it|Ganzhi|ja|干支|ka|სამოცეული ციკლი|ko|간지|mk|Шеесетгодишен циклус|ms|Ganzhi|nn|Sekstiårig syklus|no|Sekstiårig syklus|ru|Система гань-чжи|sh|Seksagenarni ciklus|simple|Sexagenary cycle|su|Daur séksagenari|sv|Himmelska stammar och jordiska grenar|th|แผนภูมิสวรรค์|tr|Altmışlık döngü|uk|Шістдесятирічний цикл|vi|Can Chi|wuu|干支|xmf|გან-ჩჟიშ სისტემა|za|Gancei|zh|干支|zh_classical|干支|zh_min_nan|Kan-chi|zh_yue|干支|qid=Q246658|lt=Sexagenary cycle}}.

It is the 1st of the sixty stem-branch combinations, preceded by {{ill|Yin Water Pig|af|Watervark (astrologie)|cdo|Gŭi-hâi|de|Wasser-Schwein|hak|Kui-hoi|ja|癸亥|ko|계해|vi|Quý Hợi|za|Gveiqhaih|zh|癸亥|zh_min_nan|Kùi-hāi|zh_yue|癸亥|qid=Q904914}} and followed by {{ill|Yin Wood Ox|ja|乙丑}}. The {{ill|Heavenly Stems|af|Hemelstam|ca|Troncs celestes|cdo|Tiĕng-găng|de|Himmelsstämme|es|Troncos celestiales|fa|شاخه‌های آسمانی|fi|Taivaalliset rungot|fr|Tige céleste|gan|天干|hak|Thiên-kôn|id|Batang Langit|it|Tronco celeste|ja|十干|ko|천간|mk|Небесни стебла|ms|Tiangan|nl|Hemelse Stammen|pl|Niebiańskie pnie|ru|Небесные стволы|tr|Göksel Gövdeler|uk|Небесні стовбури|za|Diengan|zh|天干|zh_min_nan|Thian-kan|zh_yue|天干|qid=Q1190985|lt=Heavenly Stem}} ''甲'' is Yang Wood, and the {{ill|Earthly Branches|en|Earthly Branches|qid=Q1072961|lt=Earthly Branch}} ''子'' (Rat) is Yang Water; together they form a Mutual Generation relationship in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qid=Q218652|lt=Wuxing}}.

==Months of Yang Wood Rat==
It was four years after the year of the [[:en:Metal Rooster|Metal Rooster]], the year of the {{ill|Revolution|en|Revolution|qid=Q10931|lt=Revolution}} of the {{ill|Dynasty|en|Dynasty|qid=Q164950|lt=Dynasty}} changeover, and was considered the year of the ''revolutionary decree'', or the year of many upheavals, when the {{ill|Tian|en|Tian|qid=Q1364799|lt=Tian}} will is renewed and heavenly commands are given to those who possess virtue ('''Kōji kaihatsu''''). In order to prevent this, the new year has often been held in this year since the Heian period in Japan. Since the Koshi Reform of 1024, the only year prior to the Meiji era (when the reign of the first emperor was abolished with the decree of Issei Ichigen) in which there was no Koshi Reform was in {{ill|Eiroku|ca|Eiroku|ckb|ئێیرۆکو|fa|ایروکو|fr|Ère Eiroku|ja|永禄|ko|에이로쿠|ru|Эйроку|simple|Eiroku|sr|Еироку|sv|Eiroku|tr|Eiroku|zh|永祿|qid=Q1143341|lt=Eiroku}} 7 (1564).<ref>天野忠幸によれば、将軍足利義輝と三好長慶が改元の主導権を巡って争って軍事衝突に発展することを警戒した正親町天皇が甲子改元を見送ったとする（天野忠幸『三好一族と織田信長』（戎光祥出版、2016年） ISBN 978-4-86403-185-1 P47-48）。</ref>

Emperor [[:en:Kanmu|Emperor Kanmu]] was also the son of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|en|Emperor Tenji|qid=Q314802|lt=Tenchi}}, who ascended to the throne after the {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|en|Emperor Tenmu|qid=Q335181|lt=Tenmu}} lineage was severed by the murder of his half-brother {{ill|Emperor Kōbun|en|Emperor Kōbun|qid=Q357242|lt=Otomo}}, a prince of the Tenchi line. {{ill|Emperor Kōnin|en|Emperor Kōnin|qid=Q958662|lt=Emperor Kōnin}}, and it is said that he moved the capital to [[Nagaoka-kyō|Nagaoka-kyo]] in 784, the year of the Revolution, because he was strongly aware of the change of royal line.

The {{ill|Yellow Turban Rebellion|en|Yellow Turban Rebellion|qid=Q751743|lt=Yellow Turban Rebellion}}, which occurred in 184, the last days of the Later Han Dynasty in China and determined the dissolution of the Han Dynasty, was described as "the {{Lang|zh-hant|蒼天已死 黄天當立 歳在甲子 天下大吉}}" ("Book of the Later Han|The Later Han Dynasty"). Volume 71: Huangfu Song, Zhu Shiyi, Biography 61 {{ill|Huangfu Song|en|Huangfu Song|qid=Q1120512|lt=Huang Fu Bulk}} biography<ref>{{Cite wikisource|title=後漢書/卷71|author=范曄|wslanguage=zh}}</ref>)". The slogan was.

A hot spring discovered in {{ill|Mutsu Province|en|Mutsu Province|qid=Q907389|lt=Mutsu}} (now Fukushima Prefecture) in {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|en|Nanboku-chō period|qid=Q264012|lt=Nanboku-chō period}} in 1384 was named Koshi Onsen (甲子温泉) in honor of the year Koshi.

Ito Daizo (大藏) changed his name to Ito Koshi-taro (Kashitaro/Kinetaro) in honor of the first year of [[:en:Genji (era)|Genji]] (1864), the year of the Koshi.

The baseball stadium built in {{ill|Taishō era|en|Taishō era|qid=Q329174|lt=Taisho}} 13 (1924) in {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|en|Hyōgo Prefecture|qid=Q130290|lt=Hyōgo Prefecture}} {{ill|Nishinomiya|en|Nishinomiya|qid=Q243853|lt=Nishinomiya City}} was named "Koshien Grand Sports Ground" (now {{ill|Koshien Stadium|en|Koshien Stadium|qid=Q959811|lt=Hanshin Koshien Stadium}}) after the Chinese zodiac of that year.
<ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-07-06 |title=旧・甲子園ホテル : とっておき旅 |url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/osaka/feature/kansai1308203483172_02/news/20110706-OYT8T00734.htm |access-date=2013-12-31 |website=[[読売新聞}}</ref> It is also the name of a place in the city. This year also marks the origin of the name of the Tokyo Kosha Company.
